evidence.verification: `cd research/simdesign-shellaspect && /usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 2 passed, 486 warnings, 89 s. The two tests check only that the ratio falls from l/w 3 to 6 and stays > 0.9, and that the closed form scales as 1/l^2; no test pins an FE or closed-form value against a reference. Four mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 survived (Timoshenko-Gere coefficient 4.013 -> 3.5 at eigbuckle.py:87; J correction 0.63 -> 0 at :81; every critical load x1.1 at :74), 1 caught (shear traction doubled at :42, which pushes the ratio below 0.9). A 13% error in the comparator or a 10% error in every FE result passes.
evidence.craft: Read eigbuckle.py (92 lines), scan.py, test_scan.py, pyproject.toml. Clear, short, units stated, the geometric stiffness form grad(v)_ij sigma_jk grad(u)_ik is the standard one and the shift-invert eigs is sound. Defects: eigbuckle.py is a verbatim copy of simdesign-shellorder's engine (diff identical) and its closed forms re-copy simdesign-webbuckle/ltb.py, so a fix must be made three times; `v.value[...]` at eigbuckle.py:47 raises 486 skfem DeprecationWarnings per test run; scan.py:23 writes scan.txt without a context manager; tests import by sys.path insertion rather than the declared package; pytest is not in pyproject.toml. Acceptable research code, not reviewer-clean.
evidence.claims: Every number in the README table traces to experiments/scan.txt, and research/README.md:567 and research/_homepage/projects.json:2497 quote the same percentages (pass). AI-assistance, 'stylised, preliminary', 'nothing was made or tested' and a Limitations section are present (README:3, :32-33). The attribution to shear deformation / clamp warping is explicitly labelled untested and 'a consistency check, not a demonstration' (README:28). The served page https://marisstella.app/research/simdesign-shellaspect/ returns 200 and carries the summary with 'preliminary'. One soft overreach: README:30 says the 2.1% gap at l/w = 24 'probably includes some mesh error'; an independent warping model (domain) accounts for all of it, so 'probably' is not backed. Citations (Timoshenko & Gere 1961; Gustafsson & McBain JOSS 2020) are real.
evidence.fitness: Could a researcher build on it? Yes as a reproducible data point: the scan re-runs bit-identically and the code is small. But the question it asks (why does the 3D solid exceed the slender-beam formula?) has a textbook answer it did not try: the clamp restrains warping, and Timoshenko & Gere (sec. 6.4) and Trahair (Flexural-Torsional Buckling of Structures, 1993) give the cantilever result with a warping parameter. Nearest prior work: classical LTB of narrow rectangular cantilevers (Timoshenko & Gere 1961; Hodges & Peters 1975 on pre-buckling deflection) and the many solid-vs-beam LTB verification studies; this scan is a verification exercise with no novelty claim, which the README fairly admits. One cross-section, so whether the gap is ~w/l or set by Cw/J cannot be told apart.
evidence.domain: Compared with the warping-restrained cantilever (Vlasov Cw = b^3 w^3 / 144 for a thin rectangle, theta = theta' = 0 at the clamp), solved independently by a 1D Hermite Rayleigh-Ritz (`/usr/bin/python3.13 -I /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/b2968675-933a-541b-8835-9a181e723712/scratchpad/simdesign-shellaspect/warping_fe.py`): predicted gamma_w / 4.0126 = 1.220, 1.101, 1.044, 1.021 at l/w = 3, 6, 12, 24, against the FE's 1.145, 1.074, 1.038, 1.021. At l/w >= 12 clamp warping restraint alone accounts for the whole gap (and its ~1/l scaling: K = pi sqrt(E Cw / (G J l^2)) is proportional to 1/l), and under end moment (where warping barely matters) the FE already matches the closed form to 0.3% at l/w = 12. So the README's 'could be the fixed cross-section mesh' and 'probably includes some mesh error' run against the standard theory; the right comparator was available. Not discussed either: the pre-buckling in-plane deflection effect, 1/sqrt((1-Iy/Iz)(1-GJ/EIz)) = 1.077 for this 4:1 section (Kirby & Nethercot; Trahair), which linear eigenbuckling omits and a reviewer would expect named as a limit of both models. A stability researcher would accept the numbers and reject the interpretation.

verdict: A small, honest, fully reproducible scan: three of four FE rows re-run bit-identically, the closed form re-derives to 0.014% from an independent ODE and the exact torsion series, and the same engine matches Euler and end-moment cantilever buckling within 0.5%. It misses the bar on verification (two tests, three of four seeded bugs survive, including a 13% error in the comparator and a 10% error in every FE load) and on method: the gap it sets out to explain is predicted, at l/w >= 12 to within 0.6 percentage points, by the textbook warping-restrained cantilever, which the README does not try and instead leans toward mesh error. A stability researcher would trust the numbers and rewrite the interpretation.
